title: Welcome
content: Welcome NeoPay CoreDesign: Merchant POS UI Library (CorePOS) React UI library for merchant pos. Also exposes the primitive tokens used in components. Strongly typed. Components are styled using CSS modules for isolated, scoped styling and for conditional class management and style overriding. Most, if not all, components have their base component's props spread along with a prop for extending / overriding styles. Some components have their ref forwarded (e.g. and ). The GitHub Pages Storybook deployment for this library can be viewed here . Dependencies This package was designed to be React framework-agnostic (Next.js / Electron / plain React). It only bundles essential styling utilities, You must provide / install the following peer dependencies: Installation This package is private. In order to install it you will need the access token (ask @Noah). Once you have the token, follow the instructions in the Github NPM Registries link and create a file in the consuming project's root or authenticate via the npm CLI: Usage Import Global Styles Import the bundled globals.css file in your app’s entry point to ensure core styling and fonts are applied: Wrap with GlobalUIProvider Wrap your root app component in the GlobalUIProvider. This handles global overlays like Toast and HelpModal and provides a hook for controlling them: Extending and Overriding Since the library uses , the generated class names are scoped to each component, preventing styling conflicts. However, this also means that while overriding styles is possible, it requires careful consideration on the consuming app / dev's part. : Specificity Matters: Since CSS modules generate unique identifiers for class names, custom classes may be overridden by the library's styles In order to overcome this, use more specific selectors (combining class names) if needed, or consider using the directive as a last resort Order Matters: The library components are designed to accept a prop that is appended last using from If your consuming app is configured correctly and styles are specific enough, they should take precedence If something seems off, hit up @Noah Consuming App Setup for CSS Modules Make sure the consuming app of this package supports . If using Vite, Next.js, or something similar, ensure CSS modules are enabled in your configuration: Note: Next.js supports CSS modules OOTB, but as a reminder, make you're using the correct file naming convention Example: Overriding Resources GitHub NPM Registries https://docs.github.com/en/packages/working-with-a-github-packages-registry/working-with-the-npm-registry Tailwind 4 https://tailwindcss.com/ Storybook Official Docs https://storybook.js.org/docs -- Built with 💜 by @Noah for NeoMana Labs
